skill.name: building-chat-widgets
skill.description: Build interactive ChatKit interfaces with widgets, client and server actions, entity mentions, composer tools, and streamed updates.
skill.summary: Design complete ChatKit widget lifecycles across frontend and backend.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: All static alerts are false positives from Markdown syntax, Python imports, ordinary payload fields, or a same-origin request. Three semantic risks remain: hidden context injection, an unauthorized database mutation pattern, and raw exception disclosure.

remediation.issue: Untrusted action payload enters hidden agent context.
remediation.suggestion: Validate identifiers against server-owned options, escape delimiters, and store structured trusted metadata instead of interpolating client values into model context.

remediation.issue: A confirmation action mutates data without explicit authorization.
remediation.suggestion: Authorize the current user for the target item, reject unknown identifiers, and load server-side records before calling confirm_item.

remediation.issue: The error handler returns raw exception text to users.
remediation.suggestion: Log detailed exceptions privately and return a stable generic message with a non-sensitive correlation identifier.

content.value_statement: Text-only chat cannot support structured choices, forms, or contextual actions. This skill provides ChatKit patterns for widgets, frontend handlers, backend mutations, entity mentions, and composer modes.
actual_capabilities: Creates reusable widget templates with lists, rows, text, icons, and buttons.
Connects client actions to navigation, local state changes, and follow-up chat messages.
Implements server actions that replace widgets, stream messages, and trigger client effects.
Adds searchable entity mentions and entity click handling.
Routes composer tool choices to different backend agents.
Provides a local verifier for required reference files.
limitations: Provides implementation guidance and examples, not a complete deployable application.
Assumes compatible ChatKit APIs and project-specific frontend and backend integration.
Does not supply authentication, authorization, payload schemas, or production error handling.
Requires developers to adapt storage, routing, and data models.

use_cases.title: Create Interactive Results
use_cases.description: Build list and button widgets that let users select records, open details, and request more suggestions.

use_cases.title: Handle Backend Actions
use_cases.description: Implement server handlers that mutate application data, replace widgets, and stream follow-up messages.

use_cases.title: Design Agentic Chat Workflows
use_cases.description: Combine entity mentions, composer modes, local tools, and streamed widgets into a coordinated product experience.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Basic Widget
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a ChatKit list widget with three items and one client-handled details button. Explain where each handler belongs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a simple interactive result.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Client and Server Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Add client navigation and a server confirmation action to my existing widget. Validate payload fields and show the widget replacement flow.
prompt_templates.scenario: Extend a widget with bidirectional actions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Mentions and Composer Modes
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement searchable entity mentions and two composer modes. Route each mode to the correct backend agent and describe integration points.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure Widget Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my complete ChatKit widget lifecycle. Add authorization, payload schemas, safe hidden context handling, generic errors, and tests for every action path.

output_examples.input: Build an article selection widget with client navigation.
output_examples.output: A list widget presents article titles and clear action buttons. The frontend validates each identifier before navigating to the matching internal route.

output_examples.input: Add a server confirmation action that updates the widget.
output_examples.output: The handler validates the action, authorizes the user, updates the record, replaces the widget, and sends a named client effect.

output_examples.input: Support article mentions and an event finder mode.
output_examples.output: Mention search returns labeled entities with stable identifiers. Composer metadata selects the event agent while other messages use the general agent.

best_practices: Validate every action type and payload against an explicit server-side schema.
Keep client navigation separate from authorized server-side data mutations.
Test widget rendering, action routing, replacement events, and failure responses together.
anti_patterns: Do not trust widget payload identifiers for database changes or hidden model context.
Do not process the same action in both client and server handlers.
Do not expose raw backend exceptions through assistant messages.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete chat application?
faq.answer: No. It provides integration patterns that require an existing ChatKit frontend, backend, storage layer, and application data model.

faq.question: Which action handler should I use?
faq.answer: Use client handlers for navigation and local state. Use server handlers for authorized mutations, persistence, and streamed widget updates.

faq.question: Can widgets send follow-up chat messages?
faq.answer: Yes. Client handlers can send user messages, while server handlers can create validated messages and stream response events.

faq.question: Does the skill support entity mentions?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows entity search, result mapping, click handling, and conversion of mentions into model-readable context.

faq.question: How are composer modes routed?
faq.answer: The selected tool is read from request metadata and mapped to a configured backend agent.

faq.question: What security work is still required?
faq.answer: Add authentication, authorization, strict payload validation, safe context encoding, private error logging, and tests for tampered actions.
